title: Shared transport policy for public signer-first, encrypted browser, and compatibility fallback flows
description: Reconstructed PSTF feature for Bahia's shared control-plane transport policy. This slice defines which product behaviors belong on the public signer-first relay plane, which sensitive browser behaviors must use encrypted request/result transport, which HTTP/MCP surfaces remain compatibility or tooling transports, and which legacy surfaces are present but not part of the intended contract. It also captures new HITL decisions that remove route-level REST gating from the intended browser policy, move all browser payment surfaces to encrypted transport, and classify EventSource log streaming as legacy browser behavior to remove.
dependencies: `/api/v1/system/info` as the shared discovery contract for public browser relay bootstrap, encrypted browser capability gating, and service-pubkey discovery
Canonical public control-plane kinds, encrypted operation catalog, and relay separation rules documented in `docs/control-planes.md` and `docs/nostr-commands.md`

Existing feature slices that already verify domain-specific transport behavior: `CORE_SERVICE_TO_DEPLOYMENT`, `ENCRYPTED_CONTROL_PLANE_NOTIFICATIONS`, `SIGNER_FIRST_OPERATOR_ADOPTION_RUNTIME`, `LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT`, and `SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP`
NIP-07 or NIP-46 signer identity for browser/operator flows plus explicit NIP-44 encrypt/decrypt support when encrypted browser flows are used
Event-driven Nostr semantics: subscriptions, EOSE-bounded catch-up, accepted OK handling, and no polling-based completion for canonical control-plane flows

actors.name: browser_public_flow
actors.role: loads relay-backed shared state and publishes signer-first public control-plane requests on the public browser/sidecar relay plane

actors.name: browser_encrypted_flow
actors.role: publishes encrypted request/result events for sensitive browser-visible domains and must keep those requests off the public relay plane

actors.name: operator_cli_or_admin_client
actors.role: uses signer-first public requests by default and may use explicit HTTP compatibility fallback only under bounded pre-acceptance conditions

actors.name: bahia_service
actors.role: advertises discovery metadata, enforces transport boundaries, verifies signatures and authorization, and publishes correlated status/result/read-model events

actors.name: compatibility_and_tooling_surfaces
actors.role: serve narrowed REST, direct NIP-98, and MCP needs without replacing relay-backed async truth for canonical control-plane flows

in_scope: Classification of browser-visible public signer-first flows onto public browser relays / sidecar-backed control-plane transport
Classification of sensitive browser-visible flows onto encrypted request/result transport (`5980`/`7980`) using only browser encrypted-request relays plus the Bahia service pubkey
Classification of compatibility-only HTTP behavior, including direct NIP-98-protected REST/MCP surfaces and explicit pre-acceptance operator HTTP fallback
Shared policy for deprecated or quarantined transport surfaces such as EventSource log streaming and the legacy 311xx command bridge
Cross-feature transport boundaries already implied by existing PSTF slices and the discovery contract
Browser payment and browser log-transport policy decisions captured in this reconstruction
out_of_scope: Per-domain payload schemas beyond what is needed to classify the correct transport surface
Detailed acceptance criteria or test matrices for every dependent slice
Implementation design for removing legacy transport drift
Non-browser internal service-to-service transport that is not part of the product-facing contract
Replacing the system-discovery slice itself or re-specifying all discovery fields in full

docs: `docs/control-planes.md` is the primary normative source: it defines the transport hierarchy, public request/status/result/read-model kinds, encrypted request/result contract, explicit relay separation, direct NIP-98 behavior, and deprecated legacy surfaces.

`docs/nostr-commands.md` reinforces that browser and agent consumers should subscribe for status/results/read models rather than poll REST, and it explicitly states that encrypted `5980` requests must not be sent to the public sidecar relays.
`docs/protocol-compatibility.md` now broadly agrees with the newer control-plane framing, but must still be treated as secondary because some older contradictions were called out by PSTF artifacts.

`pstf/cross_feature_analysis.md`, `pstf/spec_gap_report.md`, and `pstf/feature_backlog.json` all identify shared transport governance as a high-risk cross-feature gap rather than a single-slice detail.
code: `internal/api/handlers/system.go` advertises the public-vs-encrypted discovery inputs that every browser flow relies on: `browser_relays`, `browser_encrypted_request_relays`, `service_pubkey`, and feature gates such as `relay_read_models` and `encrypted_nostr_requests`.

`web/src/lib/nostr/encrypted-controlplane.js` enforces the browser encrypted transport boundary in code by deriving relay URLs only from `browser_encrypted_request_relays`, requiring the service pubkey, filtering correlated results by service author and requester pubkey, and rejecting publishes with no accepted OK.

`web/src/lib/auth/route-access.js` currently has an empty `ROUTE_COMPATIBILITY_REQUIREMENTS` map, which directly contradicts an older auth audit but matches the user-approved intended browser policy captured in this session.

`web/src/routes/payments/+page.svelte`, `/orgs`, and `/notifications` are currently browser-store driven for sensitive domains, while `web/src/routes/+page.svelte` still uses REST payment history for dashboard cost summary and `web/src/lib/api/client.js` still exposes EventSource log streaming and numerous REST compatibility methods.
tests: `web/tests/unit/encrypted-controlplane.test.js` proves encrypted requests use only encrypted-request relay discovery, do not treat public relays as encrypted request relays, require accepted publishes, and follow correlated encrypted results.

Existing PSTF feature slices already verify the public signer-first deployment/service flow, encrypted notifications flow, operator pre-acceptance fallback boundary, and LLM operational REST deprecation decisions, which together supply the strongest current transport evidence.

`web/tests/e2e/dashboard-smoke.spec.js` currently mocks REST `payments/history` for the dashboard cost-summary path and notes mocked EventSource-driven activity behavior, while `web/tests/unit/api-client-retry-and-edges.test.js` still unit-tests `streamLogs(...)`; those tests are evidence of observed implementation, not proof of the approved intended transport policy after this HITL pass.
issues_or_bugs: `pstf/features/SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP/hitl_decisions.md` already records open follow-up on removing direct `nostr.relays` exposure and moving operator relay visibility to NIP-51 kind `30002`.
`pstf/features/SOUL_FACTORY_PROVISIONING_TRACKING/hitl_decisions.md` already classifies timeout/relay-closure browser failure and ticker-based backend polling as FIX, not intended behavior.
existing_behavior: Bahia currently operates with a mixed transport implementation: public signer-first relay flows, encrypted browser request/result flows, narrowed REST/MCP compatibility surfaces, explicit operator HTTP fallback, and some remaining legacy browser REST/SSE usage.
The shared policy gap was real enough that the PSTF backlog explicitly promoted this new feature slice by prior HITL decision before this reconstruction pass began.

summary: Public browser/service/LLM/operator flows are implemented as signer-first Nostr request/result/read-model behavior on the public relay plane, with `/api/v1/system/info` discovery feeding relay bootstrap and kind selection.

Sensitive browser domains such as notifications, orgs, service secrets, payment history, deployment run logs, and signature verification are documented and partly implemented through encrypted `5980`/`7980` request/result flows using separate browser encrypted-request relay URLs.
Direct NIP-98-protected REST and MCP surfaces still exist for narrowed CRUD/query/log/tooling compatibility needs.
`web/src/lib/auth/route-access.js` currently applies no route-level REST compatibility gating because `ROUTE_COMPATIBILITY_REQUIREMENTS` is empty.
The `/payments` route currently uses the encrypted payments store, but the dashboard still calls REST payment history and the API client still exposes REST payment endpoints.
`web/src/lib/api/client.js` still exposes EventSource-based browser log streaming.
Legacy 311xx command handling is still present as deprecated compatibility behavior rather than fully removed implementation.

Soul Factory still contains timeout- or polling-based observed behaviors that conflict with the intended event-driven transport posture, but those behaviors were already classified as FIX in that slice.

questionable_or_legacy_behavior.behavior: An older auth audit says protected route prefixes were marked `requiresRestCompatibility`, but current route-access code leaves the compatibility map empty.
The dashboard still performs REST browser payment reads even though sensitive payment history is already modeled as an encrypted browser domain.
The browser API client still exposes EventSource-based live log streaming despite the relay-first/log-encrypted product direction.

The settings UI still expects operator relay visibility through `systemInfo.nostr.relays`, even though the approved discovery direction moved operator relay visibility away from raw discovery fields and toward the service's NIP-51 kind `30002` relay-list event.
Soul Factory still contains timeout/relay-closure and polling-based completion behavior that conflicts with the intended event-driven transport posture.

summary: Bahia's canonical public control-plane contract is signer-first, relay-backed, and event-driven: browser and operator clients should publish signed public request kinds, require accepted relay OK responses, follow correlated status/result events, and derive shared state from relay-backed read models rather than REST writes or polling.

Sensitive browser-visible domains belong on encrypted `5980`/`7980` request/result transport and must use only `browser_encrypted_request_relays` plus the Bahia service pubkey; sensitive payloads must never be published to the public browser/sidecar relay plane.
Direct NIP-98-protected REST and MCP surfaces may remain as narrowed compatibility/query/tooling transports, but they do not replace relay-backed async truth for canonical control-plane workflows.
Route-level REST compatibility gating is not part of the intended browser policy today; the empty route-level compatibility map is approved and the older audit statement is stale.
All browser-visible payment surfaces should move to encrypted transport. Remaining browser REST payment reads are legacy drift to fix or remove rather than intended coexistence.

EventSource-based browser log streaming is not part of the intended browser transport contract and should be treated as legacy behavior to deprecate in favor of approved Nostr-native or encrypted log flows.
Operator-facing relay visibility should come from the service's NIP-51 kind `30002` relay-list event rather than raw `systemInfo.nostr.relays` discovery fields.

Operational REST mutation surfaces already removed by prior HITL decisions, such as the flagged LLM operational REST endpoints, are not part of the intended long-term product contract even if legacy code paths remain behind flags.

Explicit compatibility exceptions are still allowed when already approved elsewhere: for example, operator HTTP fallback may exist only as explicit pre-acceptance compatibility mode and must never activate after any relay accepted the signer-first request.
Event-driven transport governance applies across feature families: timeout- or polling-based completion logic is not normative behavior for relay-backed flows.

preconditions: `/api/v1/system/info` advertises coherent public and encrypted browser discovery metadata consistent with the system-discovery slice.
The requester is using an authenticated signer session for browser/operator Nostr flows.
Encrypted browser flows have access to a signer mode that exposes the required NIP-44 encrypt/decrypt capability.
Compatibility surfaces that remain in use are explicitly documented as compatibility/tooling behavior rather than silently standing in for canonical control-plane completion.
postconditions: A given user-visible workflow is classifiable onto one approved transport surface rather than relying on accidental coexistence.
Sensitive browser payloads stay off the public relay plane.
Canonical async completion for public and encrypted Nostr flows is derived from correlated events, accepted OK handling, and open subscriptions rather than HTTP polling or arbitrary browser timeouts.
Legacy browser REST/SSE drift is called out explicitly instead of being preserved silently.

happy_paths.title: Public signer-first browser flow stays on the public relay plane
steps: Browser bootstraps from `/api/v1/system/info`, resolves public browser relays, and loads relay-backed shared state until EOSE.
Browser publishes a signed public request kind such as service/deployment/LLM/operator action.
At least one relay accepts the publish and the client follows correlated status/result events plus later read-model projections.
No REST mutation or encrypted request transport is used as the canonical completion path for that public workflow.

happy_paths.title: Sensitive browser flow stays on encrypted request/result transport
steps: Browser reads `browser_encrypted_request_relays`, `service_pubkey`, and `features.encrypted_nostr_requests` from system discovery.
Browser encrypts a `5980` request to the Bahia service pubkey and publishes only to the encrypted-request relay set.
Browser ignores unrelated or spoofed results and resolves only a correlated encrypted `7980` terminal result from the Bahia service author.
Sensitive domain data remains absent from public relay read-model traffic.

happy_paths.title: Compatibility fallback remains explicit and bounded
steps: An operator client attempts the canonical signer-first public request flow.
Only if no relay accepts the request and fallback was explicitly requested may the client use HTTP compatibility fallback.
Once any relay accepted the signer-first request, terminal failure remains terminal and must not flip into HTTP fallback.

failure_paths.title: Sensitive browser payload published to public relays
failure_paths.behavior: If a sensitive browser-visible workflow uses public browser relays instead of encrypted request relays, that is a transport-policy violation rather than an alternate approved path.

failure_paths.title: Legacy browser REST payment reads treated as approved behavior
failure_paths.behavior: Browser payment history or equivalent browser-visible payment reads must not rely on REST as part of the intended product contract after HITL-TRANSPORT_POLICY_GOVERNANCE-002.

failure_paths.title: EventSource browser log streaming treated as approved transport
failure_paths.behavior: EventSource-based browser log streaming is not an approved browser transport surface after HITL-TRANSPORT_POLICY_GOVERNANCE-003 and should be treated as legacy drift.

failure_paths.title: Compatibility fallback activated after signer-first request acceptance
failure_paths.behavior: HTTP fallback after any relay accepted a signer-first request violates the approved transport boundary for public operator flows.

failure_paths.title: Timeout- or polling-based completion substituted for event-driven truth
failure_paths.behavior: For canonical relay-backed flows, arbitrary timeout or polling logic is not an approved substitute for subscriptions, EOSE, OK handling, and correlated terminal events.

edge_cases: NIP-46 signer support is not by itself sufficient for encrypted browser flows unless the provider exposes NIP-44 encrypt/decrypt capability to the web app.
Legacy 311xx command handling may remain present in code, but it is compatibility-only and must not be promoted back to the intended primary contract.
Discovery terminology must not misclassify encryption as a relay type; encrypted behavior is an event-level property with separate discovery/gating inputs, consistent with prior HITL decisions.
Operator relay visibility should not depend on raw `systemInfo.nostr.relays` exposure in the intended contract after the system-discovery decisions that move this toward NIP-51 kind `30002`.
non_functional_requirements: Transport governance must preserve Bahia's Nostr-native event-driven semantics: subscribe and react, use EOSE for historical catch-up, and verify accepted publishes plus correlated results rather than polling for completion.
Public and encrypted browser relay sets must remain distinct security boundaries.
Sensitive browser-visible data must never leak onto public sidecar/browser relays as plaintext or public read-model payloads.
Legacy compatibility surfaces must be explicit and narrow; they must not silently re-become the canonical product contract through implementation drift.
Cross-feature transport rules must remain stable enough that new encrypted or signer-first slices can inherit them instead of redefining them ad hoc.

contradictions_and_gaps.note: The signer-first auth audit says route-level REST compatibility gating was added, but current code leaves the compatibility map empty; this reconstruction classifies the audit note as stale rather than preserving the contradiction as intended behavior.

Browser payment transport is still mixed in implementation because dashboard cost summary uses REST payment history even though the intended browser policy now requires encrypted transport for all browser payment surfaces.
EventSource browser log streaming still exists in the API client, but the intended browser transport contract now excludes it.
The portfolio still lacks a single mixed-transport browser proof that one authenticated session can execute both public and encrypted journeys while preserving relay separation end to end.

Legacy 311xx compatibility handling and the still-unmigrated settings-page relay-visibility expectation both need cleanup or stronger quarantine so the intended transport policy is not ambiguous in future slices.
